description: We are Signature Developers, a team of passionate students interested in coding, software development, innovation, and space exploration. We aim to combine creativity and technology to develop an innovative solution for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.
summary:
Our project identifies and maps terrestrial analog sites on Earth that closely replicate the geological, environmental, and extreme surface conditions of permanent Moon base locations and Mars landing zones. By analyzing remote sensing data, terrain elevation, and climate metrics, we developed a framework to pinpoint Earth-based testing grounds that mirror lunar craters, regolith compositions, and Martian deserts.
This solution directly addresses the challenge of preparing for deep-space exploration without incurring the extreme costs and risks of off-world trial runs. Having verified analog locations allows scientists and engineers to rigorously test rovers, life-support habitats, and astronaut exploration protocols in realistic conditions before launch. Ultimately, this research is vital for reducing mission failure risks, accelerating space technology readiness, and ensuring crew safety as humanity prepares for sustained planetary settlement
details: Our project identifies Earth-based analog sites that closely replicate the terrain and environmental conditions of potential permanent bases on the Moon and Mars. By mapping these locations, scientists and engineers can safely test space equipment, prototype habitats, and refine exploration strategies before deploying astronauts on deep-space missions.
